battle.name: 伊奧尼亞起義
battle.brief: 公元前499年，伊奧尼亞同盟在米利都起兵，聯軍夜襲薩迪斯未果，前493年在拉代海峽敗於波斯水師，米利都隨之淪陷。卡面的埃及長矛屬早王朝型制，比這場戰爭早約二千七百年，並未出現在米利都城牆與拉代島上。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 公元前499年爆發於小亞細亞西岸的伊奧尼亞起義，交戰雙方並非對等的國家，而是一個希臘城邦聯盟對抗阿契美尼德波斯帝國。起義方是伊奧尼亞同盟的城邦：米利都、米尼、普里耶涅、泰奧斯、厄律特里亞、克利佐美奈、福凱亞、以弗所、薩摩斯，以及萊斯波斯島上的米提利尼與 Methymna。這些城市在波斯統治下多由「僭主」或寡頭議事會治理，須向薩迪斯的總督繳付貢賦，並提供水手、兵員與船隻。運動的核心是米利都的米爾姆納德王朝僭主阿里斯塔戈拉斯；他在波斯宮廷任命的米利都僭主希斯提亞斯被扣押之後，兩人聯手把抗訴變成了起兵。城邦內部另有主張恢復自治的民主派，與留在波斯陣營的寡頭彼此對立。外部援助有限但關鍵：雅典派出二十艘船與五名將領，埃雷特里亞派出五艘船，其他希臘城邦的援軍因路途遙遠未能及時抵達；羅得斯與克里特明確不參與。鎮壓方是波斯帝國：國王大流士一世坐鎮薩迪斯，呂底亞總督阿塔弗爾涅斯主持城防與行政，海軍由波斯裔將領歐塔涅斯與達提斯率領，艦隊由腓尼基人、塞浦路斯人、呂基亞人以及愛奧尼亞地區留居波斯一方者湊成。波斯陸軍並非單一民族，除波斯人與米底人外，還徵發薩卡人、薩塔吉底亞人、呂底亞人、密西亞人、佛里吉亞人與卡皮斯人等部族，配以大量以弓矢為主的遠射兵。力量對比極為懸殊：起義方倚靠城牆、船隊與對鄉土地形的熟悉，波斯方倚靠二十萬量級的步兵、三萬量級的騎兵、六百艘戰船，以及圍困米利都所需的封鎖與攻城能力。
countriesEn: The Ionian Revolt broke out on the western coast of Asia Minor in 499 BC, and the two sides were not equal states but a league of Greek poleis set against the Achaemenid Persian Empire. The insurgents were the cities of the Ionian League: Miletus, Myus, Priene, Teos, Erythrae, Clazomenae, Phocaea, Ephesus, Samos, and Mytilene and Methymna on the island of Lesbos. Under Persian rule these cities were mostly governed by tyrants or oligarchic councils, paid tribute to the satrap at Sardis, and supplied sailors, troops and ships. The driving force of the movement was Aristagoras of Miletus, of the Mermnad dynasty; after Histiaeus, the Persian-appointed tyrant of Miletus, was detained at Sardis, the two of them turned a complaint into an armed rising. Within the cities a democratic faction favouring a restoration of autonomy faced oligarchs who stayed on the Persian side. Outside help was limited but decisive: Athens sent twenty ships with five commanders and Eretria sent five, while aid from other Greek cities failed to arrive in time; Rhodes and Crete held clearly apart. The side that suppressed the revolt was the Persian Empire: King Darius I remained at Sardis, the satrap of Lydia Artaphernes administered the city and its defences, and the fleet was led by Persian commanders Otanes and Datis, its hulls supplied by Phoenicians, Cypriots, Lycians and by those Ionian districts that stayed with Persia. The Persian land army was not a single people: besides Persians and Medes it drew on Sacae, Sattagydiae, Lydians, Mysians, Phrygians and Caspians, with large numbers of missile troops whose weapon was the bow. The balance of force was overwhelming against the insurgents: they relied on their walls, their ships and their knowledge of the local ground, while the Persians relied on infantry numbered in the region of two hundred thousand, cavalry in the region of thirty thousand, six hundred warships, and the means to blockade and assault Miletus.
people: 起義方的關鍵人物集中在一個家族與兩位領袖身上。阿里斯塔戈拉斯是米利都的僭主，出身於曾統治米利都的米爾姆納德王朝；前499年他奉命率軍遠征納克索斯，以扶植對波斯俯順的寡頭取代當地民主派，結果一敗而幾乎喪盡艦隊，深怕大流士追罪，遂決定先發制人。他於某夜率部眾奪取米利都城門、封閉出入口，並以一封假造的消息煽動各城，宣稱雅典已出手相助；米利都上城的人逃往米卡萊山脊，下城被焚。希斯提亞斯是波斯所任命的米利都僭主，也是大流士的近臣；他被阿塔弗爾涅斯扣在薩迪斯後，設法遞信給阿里斯塔戈拉斯，成為起義的導火線；米卡萊之役後他仍留在愛奧尼亞。米卡萊會盟中出謀策劃的還有雅典人米太亞德，他率領雅典的二十艘船參與其事，把米利都的攻勢一路帶到薩迪斯；米利都市場上為他立碑記事，後來他在希波戰爭中名聲更盛。城內另有反波斯的民主派與薩迪斯城中的卡比爾人響應者，卡比爾人曾為夜襲者開啟城門。波斯方面的核心人物是國王大流士一世、呂底亞總督阿塔弗爾涅斯，以及海軍統帥歐塔涅斯與達提斯。戰後薩迪斯宮中的阿托莎為伊奧尼亞各城求情，被囚的斯巴達王德馬拉圖斯則勸波斯人讓流亡者返回重建家園，此議最終被採納，阿里斯塔戈拉斯事後流亡色雷斯、轉入卡里亞，最終在卡里亞被對抗的卡里亞人殺死；希斯提亞斯被俘後在薩迪斯失去信用，最後被阿塔弗爾涅斯處死。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the insurgent side were concentrated in one family and two leaders. Aristagoras was the tyrant of Miletus, born of the Mermnad dynasty that had ruled the city; in 499 BC he was ordered to lead an expedition against Naxos in order to replace the local democrats with an oligarchy obedient to Persia, and the force was defeated and its fleet almost wiped out, so fearing punishment from Darius he resolved to strike first. On a certain night he seized the gates of Miletus with his followers, closed the entrances, and stirred the cities with a forged message claiming that Athens had already given its support; the Milesians in the upper town fled to the heights of Mycale and the lower town was fired. Histiaeus was the Persian-appointed tyrant of Miletus and a confidant of Darius; after he was detained by Artaphernes at Sardis he managed to send word to Aristagoras, and that message was the spark of the revolt; after the affair at Mycale he remained in Ionia. A further brain of the Mycale scheme was the Athenian Miltiades, who led the twenty Athenian ships in the enterprise and carried the offensive from Miletus as far as Sardis; a pillar was set up for him in the market-place of Miletus, and he became far better known later during the Persian wars. Within the cities there were also anti-Persian democrats, and the Carians inside Sardis answered the rising by opening the gates to the attackers. On the Persian side the central figures were King Darius I, the satrap of Lydia Artaphernes, and the naval commanders Otanes and Datis. After the war Atossa interceded in the court at Sardis for the Ionian cities, and the exiled Spartan king Demaratus urged the Persians to let the exiles return and rebuild their homes; the proposal was eventually adopted. Aristagoras afterwards fled to Thrace and then to Caria, where he was killed by Carians who had taken up arms against him; Histiaeus was taken alive, lost the trust of Sardis and was finally put to death on the orders of Artaphernes.
kits: 卡面兵器是「埃及長矛」：早王朝時期以銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上的長矛，供守城與野戰時戳刺、格擋。它比這場起義早了約二千七百年，並不出現在米利都的城牆上，這一點必須先講清楚。把它放進這場戰爭，是因為它標示出冷兵器中最古老、也最普遍的一支技術譜系：木杆前端裝金屬矛頭，靠戳、擋與投擲發揮作用；而起義方的希臘重裝步兵恰恰是這支譜系的高階形態，以列陣互相推壓、掩體與掩護下的戳刺取勝。起義軍與盟軍的裝備以重裝步兵為主：白楊木製的長矛，矛杆約兩公尺，矛尖為青銅或鐵質加一片狹長矛葉，矛身中段常繫皮條，作用一是加固矛尖，二是供後列士兵在推盾前進時抓握；正面用「阿爾戈斯式」圓形大盾，盾面覆青銅並帶中央突角，背面有雙把手；身穿亞麻布製的胸甲與頸甲，頭戴青銅頭盔，配皮制綁腿與護臂，另有短劍與兩三支輕型投槍。米利都城牆按希羅多德的記述呈環形，設有九座城門，牆體以石砌並沿山勢收束，攻城方必須逐段突破。波斯方面是全套軍備：柳條編織再覆皮的圓盾，弓手用複合弓配箭袋，步兵用短矛與斧，鎧甲為魚鱗式鱗甲，頭盔為帶護頰的尖頂或盆形盔；軍隊另備車輛作為圍城與後勤的載具，並有大量以弓為主的部族兵。海上方面是關鍵：雙方都是三列槍座戰船為主力，輔以雙列槍座船與圓形五十人船，配撞角、舷梯與登船用的接舷板，靠划槳、順風揚帆與接舷登船取勝。伊奧尼亞方在數週之內新造上百艘戰船，並在拉代島集結；波斯方則以六百艘的混合艦隊從海上包圍米利都，切斷城與盟邦的聯繫。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian spear: a spear of the Early Dynastic period with a copper or bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft, used for stabbing and bracing in the defence of walls and in the open field. It predates this revolt by roughly two thousand seven hundred years and did not appear on the walls of Miletus, and that has to be said first. It is placed in this war because it marks the oldest and most widespread family of cold weapons, the spear, made of a wooden shaft with a metal head at the front and worked by stabbing, parrying and throwing; and the Greek hoplites of the insurgents were precisely the advanced form of that same family, winning by shoving against one another in line, stabbing under the protection of shields and of the covering formation. The equipment of the insurgents and their allies was based on the hoplite: an ash-wood spear about two metres long, with a bronze or iron head and a narrow blade, and often a thong bound round the middle of the shaft, both to stiffen the head and to give the rear rank something to grip as they pressed forward behind their shields; a large round Argive shield faced with bronze and furnished with a central boss, with a double grip on the inside; a linen corselet and neck guard, a bronze helmet, leather greaves and arm guards, with a short sword and two or three light javelins besides. The wall of Miletus, according to Herodotus, ran in a circuit with nine gates, built of stone and closing around the rise of the ground, so that an assaulting force had to work its way forward section by section. The Persians brought the full military set: round shields of wicker covered with hide, composite bows and quivers for the archers, short spears and axes for the foot, scale armour, and helmets with cheek pieces of the pointed or kettle type; the host also carried wagons for the siege and the baggage, together with large numbers of troops whose principal weapon was the bow. At sea the deciding factor was the trireme: both sides fought mainly with three-banked vessels, supported by biremes and fifty-oared round ships, fitted with rams, boarding ladders and gangplanks, and fought by rowing, running before the wind and boarding hand to hand. The Ionians built more than a hundred warships within a few weeks and mustered them on the island of Lade; the Persians, with a mixed fleet of six hundred hulls, invested Miletus from the sea and cut the city off from its allies.
tactics: 起義的戰術主軸有三段，各段做法不同。夜襲米利都靠的是內應與時機：阿里斯塔戈拉斯選擇夜間進攻，奪門後立即封閉城門，把城分成上下兩部，上城的守軍退往米卡萊山脊，義軍則在城內縱火。攻薩迪斯是一次強行晝行後的急襲：聯軍自米利都出發，走山路與驛道，以夜行抵達薩迪斯城郊，突入城區後包圍總督府邸，放火焚燒，並驅散城中的守備；結果薩迪斯城內的卡比爾人反而打開城門接應，波斯援軍及時趕到把義軍逐出城區，聯軍才得以退回海邊的船隊。第二次攻薩迪斯的計劃則更宏大：義軍約定在米卡萊集結，以樹上懸掛花環為信號，然後直取薩迪斯，奪取總督的堡壘；計劃被以弗所方面察覺，以弗所人封住通往薩迪斯的山道設伏，義軍在山中被截擊潰散，撤退時由雅典的二十艘船接應掩護。米卡萊的失敗之後，起義轉為以海軍為核心的消耗戰：雙方在拉代島外排成戰線互相衝撞，試圖以撞角擊穿對方水線、然後接舷登船殲滅敵人。伊奧尼亞方在連日交戰中由整列轉為各自應戰，陣形一旦鬆動便紛紛逃回本城；波斯方則集中腓尼基與塞浦路斯艦隊追擊殘餘船隻，奪船者斬首示眾。最終攻取米利都時，波斯軍不再強攻城牆，而是圍城築牆、掘地道、封鎖港池，斷絕城內的糧食與援兵，數月之後城內撐不住，加上以弗所人的勸降，米利都開城投降，普里耶涅也隨之屈服。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of the revolt runs through three phases, each with its own method. The night attack on Miletus depended on inside help and on timing: Aristagoras chose to strike by night, seized the gates and at once shut them, divided the town into an upper and a lower part, drove the defenders of the upper town back to the heights of Mycale, and fired the lower town. The move on Sardis was a forced march followed by a sudden assault: the allied column set out from Miletus, took the mountain paths and the post road, reached the outskirts of Sardis by a night march, pushed into the city, surrounded the satrap's palace, set it on fire and drove off the garrison; instead the Carians inside Sardis opened the gates to the attackers, and the timely arrival of Persian reinforcements drove the insurgents back out of the city, so that they were able to withdraw to their ships on the shore. The second scheme against Sardis was far larger in scale: the insurgents were to muster on Mycale, with a garland hung on a tree as the signal, and then go straight for Sardis to seize the satrap's citadel; the plan was detected from the Ephesian side, the Ephesians blocked the mountain road to Sardis and ambushed the column, the insurgents were cut up in the hills, and the Athenian twenty ships covered the retreat. After the failure at Mycale the revolt turned into a naval war fought around attrition: the two fleets formed line abreast in the strait off Lade, trying to sink the enemy's waterline with the ram and then board him hand to hand. Over successive days the Ionian line dissolved into separate squadrons, and once the formation loosened the ships fled each to its own city; the Persians concentrated their Phoenician and Cypriot squadrons against the remainder, and those who took a ship cut off the heads of the crews for display. For the final reduction of Miletus the Persians no longer assaulted the wall directly: they ringed the city with a circuit of earthworks, drove mines under the defences, sealed the harbour, cut off food and reinforcements, and after a number of months the city could hold out no longer; with the Ephesians urging surrender, Miletus opened its gates and Priene followed.
data: 可核實的數字集中在兵力與船數上。公元前499年遠征納克索斯的聯合艦隊，波斯方面出二百艘、愛奧尼亞方面出二百艘，結果失利，戰船折損大半。雅典援助伊奧尼亞的船數為二十艘，埃雷特里亞為五艘，兩者的水手在薩迪斯城下被波斯人俘獲。拉代海戰的雙方艦隊數目有明確記載：伊奧尼亞方面共約一百二十艘三列槍座戰船，以米利都製造的數量最多，其餘各城按人口比例分攤，福凱亞與薩摩斯不參戰；波斯方面為六百艘，包括腓尼基、塞浦路斯、呂基亞與留居波斯一方的愛奧尼亞船隻。同一場戰役中波斯投入的陸軍，步兵約二十萬、騎兵約三萬，各部族兵員由數千至數萬不等，另有攻城與後勤車輛若干。戰事曆時方面，希羅多德把波斯攻取米利都記在起義的第六年，即前493年；從前499年起兵到米利都淪陷，前後約六年，圍城歷時數月。城防與地理數字亦可核對：米利都城牆呈環形、設九座城門；米利都與薩迪斯之間按現代測算直線約一百公里，因此夜行急襲必須在拂曉前完成。薩摩斯與拉代島之間的海峽水域狹窄，東風起時帆船容易失速，這是義軍在海戰中失利的自然條件之一。米利都陷落後，約三萬名米利都市民被擄往蘇薩為奴，此為希羅多德留下的數字。起義各城的具體人口數字沒有可靠記錄，古代作者多用「眾多」形容，不能當作精確的產能或人口數字使用。
dataEn: The verifiable figures cluster around troops and ships. In the expedition against Naxos in 499 BC the combined fleet was two hundred vessels from the Persian side and two hundred from the Ionian side, and it failed, losing the greater part of its ships. The Athenian aid to Ionia was twenty ships and the Eretrian aid five, and their crews were taken by the Persians under the walls of Sardis. The numbers in the battle of Lade are explicitly recorded: the Ionian side mustered about one hundred and twenty triremes, the greater share built at Miletus and the remainder allotted to the other cities according to size, with Phocaea and Samos abstaining; the Persian side numbered six hundred hulls, Phoenician, Cypriot, Lycian and Ionian ships of those who had stayed with Persia. In the same campaign the Persians committed land forces of about two hundred thousand foot and about thirty thousand horse, the contingents of the various peoples running from several thousand to several tens of thousands apiece, together with a number of wagons for the siege and the baggage. On duration, Herodotus dates the capture of Miletus to the sixth year of the revolt, that is 493 BC; from the rising of 499 BC to the fall of Miletus there were about six years, and the siege itself lasted a number of months. The figures of fortification and geography can also be checked: the wall of Miletus ran in a circuit with nine gates, and by modern measurement the straight line from Miletus to Sardis is about one hundred kilometres, so that a night march and assault had to be completed before dawn. The strait between Samos and the island of Lade is narrow, and vessels running before an east wind lose their steerage easily, which is one of the natural conditions behind the Ionian defeat at sea. After the fall of Miletus about thirty thousand Milesians were carried off to Susa as slaves, and this is the figure Herodotus preserves. No reliable figures survive for the populations of the individual Ionian cities; the ancient writers habitually describe them as numerous, and such descriptions cannot be used as precise measures of population or output.
cause: 起義的成因可以分成遠因、近因與直接引信三層。最遠的一層是波斯的征服：前546年居魯士滅呂底亞，小亞細亞西岸的希臘城邦隨即淪為帝國邊境屬地。波斯帶來的統治比呂底亞更嚴苛，薩迪斯的總督按城徵收貢賦，愛奧尼亞城市既要交出錢財，也要提供水手、稅款與兵力；狄迪瑪的阿波羅神廟被焚，神廟轄地與祭司的傳統受到直接侵犯，知識階層把這件事視為文化上的毀滅。城邦精英長期以「自由而富庶」自居，波斯的稅制與駐軍卻抽走了這份富庶。伊奧尼亞各城內部又分為民主派與寡頭派，前者認為起兵才有出路，後者則靠波斯總督維持現狀，這條裂縫使起兵一旦成功便迅速擴散。第二層是外部的偶然條件：公元前六世紀末伊奧尼亞城邦正處於希臘世界走向波斯的邊緣，雅典與埃雷特里亞派出船隊，既有同族與同宗教的關係，也有打擊波斯的算計，這批船隻在米利都提供了海軍骨幹，也讓義軍相信可以得到外援。第三層是直接引信：前499年阿里斯塔戈拉斯率領雙方各二百艘戰船遠征納克索斯失利，損失慘重，他深恐大流士追究，於是決定先發制人，用一封假造的消息宣稱雅典已出手相助，藉此繞過各城的猶豫，把一場外交抗訴變成全面叛亂。
causeEn: The causes of the revolt divide into remote causes, proximate causes and an immediate trigger. The remotest is the Persian conquest: in 546 BC Cyrus destroyed Lydia, and the Greek cities of the western coast of Asia Minor fell at once into the empire's frontier zone. Persian rule was harsher than Lydian: the satrap at Sardis levied tribute city by city, and the Ionian cities had to give up money, but also crews, taxes and soldiers; the temple of Apollo at Didyma was burned, the property of the sanctuary and the position of its priesthood were directly violated, and the literate classes treated the deed as a cultural catastrophe. The elites of the Ionian cities had long described themselves as free and wealthy, and the Persian tax system and garrison drained that wealth away. Within each city the line ran between democrats and oligarchs, the former convinced that only a rising could open a way out, the latter sustained by the satrap in their position, and that fault line meant that once a rising began it spread quickly. The second layer consists of external circumstance: at the end of the sixth century BC the Ionian cities stood on the edge between the Greek world and Persia, and the squadrons sent by Athens and Eretria were moved both by kinship and religion and by the calculation of striking at Persia; those ships gave the rising a naval backbone at Miletus and persuaded the insurgents that help would come. The third layer is the immediate trigger: in 499 BC Aristagoras led the joint force of two hundred ships a side against Naxos and was badly defeated with heavy losses, and fearing that Darius would call him to account he struck first, using a forged message that claimed Athens had already given its aid, so as to carry the cities past their hesitation and turn a diplomatic complaint into a general rebellion.
impact: 起義雖然失敗，卻徹底改變了愛琴海東岸的權力格局，也把波斯與希臘的衝突推上一個新台階。首當其衝的是伊奧尼亞各城：戰後城牆被拆、港口封閉、居民被擄往蘇薩，愛奧尼亞同盟的城邦從名義上的自治成員，變成帝國直接派總督管轄的行政單位，貢賦與兵員的徵發被固定下來；大流士一度打算徹底拆毀這些城，經阿托莎求情與德馬拉圖斯的建議後改為准許流亡者返回重建，使波斯得以在同一批城裡維持稅源與海軍徵召的基地。希臘城邦之間的裂痕同樣加深：援助起義的雅典與埃雷特里亞遭到報復，羅得斯與克里特保持中立，此後希臘人在波斯問題上的分裂，成為兩方交鋒時的固定變數。流亡者的去向也留下痕跡，埃雷特里亞的倖存者被安置在雅典的埃琉西斯，薩摩斯的流亡者後來由雅典給予公民權，福凱亞人遷往意大利的傳說則把伊奧尼亞的名字帶到羅馬的城郊地帶。戰爭在希臘本土的直接後果，是前490年大流士為懲罰雅典與埃雷特里亞而發動的遠征，以及馬拉松的戰役，接著便是前480年薛西斯的大舉入侵；伊奧尼亞的沙場因此成為希波戰爭的前傳，希臘人的集體記憶也把它記成希臘自由與亞洲專制衝突的第一次大碰撞。在軍事技術上，拉代海戰是愛琴海最早、也最完整被記錄的艦隊決戰之一，撞角衝撞加接舷登船的希臘式海戰套路由此定型，而聯盟式海軍缺乏統一指揮、各城各自求生的弱點也在這一戰暴露無遺。
impactEn: The revolt failed, yet it completely rearranged the balance of power on the eastern shore of the Aegean and raised the collision between Persia and Greece to a new level. The Ionian cities bore the first blow: after the war their walls were torn down, their harbours closed and their inhabitants carried off to Susa, and the members of the Ionian League passed from nominal autonomy into administrative units under governors appointed by the empire, with tribute and military service fixed as a standing arrangement; Darius had at one point intended to demolish the cities outright, and after Atossa's intercession and Demaratus's advice he allowed the exiles to return and rebuild, so that Persia kept the same cities as a base of taxation and of naval recruitment. The fissure between the Greek cities widened as well: Athens and Eretria, which had aided the revolt, were punished, while Rhodes and Crete stood apart, and from then on the division of the Greeks on the Persian question became a fixed variable in every coming clash. The fate of the exiles left its mark too: the survivors of Eretria were settled at Eleusis in Athenian territory, the Samians were later granted citizenship by Athens, and the tradition of the Phocaeans migrating to Italy carried the Ionian name into the outskirts of Rome. The direct consequence on the Greek mainland was Darius's expedition of 490 BC, sent to punish Athens and Eretria, and the battle of Marathon, and then the great invasion of Xerxes in 480 BC; the Ionian theatre thus became the prelude to the Persian Wars, and Greek collective memory recorded it as the first great collision between Hellenic freedom and Asian despotism. In military technology the battle of Lade is among the earliest and the most completely recorded fleet actions in the Aegean, and the Greek pattern of ramming and boarding was fixed by it, while the weakness of a league navy without unified command, each city saving itself, was exposed in the same battle.
result: 前493年，米利都投降，普里耶涅隨之屈服，起義以城邦聯盟的潰散告終。米利都開城之後，環形的城牆被推倒，港口被封鎖，城中的船隻與裝備被波斯人收繳，約三萬名米利都市民被擄往蘇薩；拉代海戰中伊奧尼亞方面的百餘艘戰船，或沉或被奪，留在島上的守軍四散。首腦人物的下場各不相同：阿里斯塔戈拉斯輾轉流亡色雷斯與卡里亞，最後被起而反抗的卡里亞人殺死；希斯提亞斯被俘後在薩迪斯失去大流士的信任，最後被阿塔弗爾涅斯處死；為義軍作戰的雅典與埃雷特里亞的船隊則在水路與薩迪斯城下被波斯人俘獲。戰後大流士本欲把伊奧尼亞各城徹底剷平，因阿托莎的求情與德馬拉圖斯的勸說而改為准許重建，並以總督分區管治，同時把雅典與埃雷特里亞列入懲罰名單，於是有了前490年的遠征與馬拉松之戰。就戰爭本身而言，聯盟式起義未能保住任何城邦的自主，卻迫使波斯改以帝國直轄的方式治理這片海岸，並把一次邊境上的騷動變成了半個世紀希臘與波斯全面戰爭的起點；就武器史而言，這場戰爭同時記錄了長矛技術的兩端：卡面那件早王朝的埃及長矛，與前493年仍在拉代海峽列陣的希臘重裝步兵長矛，兩者相隔約二千七百年，中間卻是同一條金屬矛頭加木杆的技術譜系一路走到成熟的戰役。
resultEn: In 493 BC Miletus surrendered, Priene yielded in the same way, and the revolt ended in the dissolution of the league. After Miletus opened its gates the circuit of its wall was pulled down, the harbour was sealed, the ships and the equipment of the city were taken over by the Persians, and about thirty thousand Milesians were carried off to Susa as slaves; of the Ionian fleet of more than a hundred warships, those that had not sunk were captured, and the garrisons left on the island scattered. The fates of the leaders differed: Aristagoras wandered into exile in Thrace and then Caria and was finally killed by Carians who had risen against him; Histiaeus was taken alive, lost Darius's trust at Sardis and was put to death on the orders of Artaphernes; and the Athenian and Eretrian squadrons that had fought for the insurgents were captured by the Persians at sea and under the walls of Sardis. After the war Darius had intended to raze the Ionian cities to the ground, but on Atossa's intercession and Demaratus's advice he allowed them to be rebuilt and put them under governors appointed from the Persian side, while at the same time placing Athens and Eretria on the list of those to be punished, which produced the expedition of 490 BC and the battle of Marathon. As a war, the league rising saved no city's independence, but it forced Persia to govern that coast directly as part of the empire, and turned a disturbance on a frontier into the opening of half a century of general war between Greece and Persia. In the history of weapons the same conflict records the two ends of the spear: the Egyptian spear of the Early Dynastic period on the card, and the hoplite spears still drawn up in line in the strait of Lade in 493 BC, some twenty-seven hundred years apart, but joined by one continuous lineage of a metal head fixed to a wooden shaft.
